title: Requests & approvals
summary: Build editable requests, review assignments, revision-bound decisions, delegation, and an audit timeline.
outcome: An approval app where reviewers approve a specific revision and concurrent or unauthorized decisions cannot silently win.
prerequisites: Typed domain errors, verified roles, optimistic concurrency, and transactional audit events. Use a simple equipment-request domain.
model: Request: id, requesterId, title, justification, status, revision. Submission: requestId, immutable revision snapshot.
ReviewAssignment: submissionId, reviewerId, state. Decision: submissionId, actorId, result, reason, operationId.
Delegation: delegator, delegate, scope, startsAt, endsAt. AuditEvent records submitted, withdrawn, delegated, and decided actions.
boundaries: Request editor → submission service → immutable review snapshot → authorized decision transaction → notification outbox.

milestones.title: Create drafts and immutable submissions
milestones.brief: Let requesters edit drafts freely while giving reviewers a stable snapshot of the submitted request.
milestones.explanation: A reviewer must know exactly what they are deciding on. If a mutable draft changes underneath an approval screen, the stored decision can refer to content the reviewer never saw. Model submission as an explicit operation that captures a revision, and define whether changes after submission require withdrawal or a new submission.
steps: Write draft, submit, withdraw, and resubmit examples. Specify required fields only at the stages where the business needs them.
Implement draft CRUD and an atomic submission snapshot. Display draft versus submitted content clearly and preserve both identities.
Test missing required data, repeated submit, and an edit arriving while submission is in progress.

checks.label: Drafts can be saved under the documented partial-data rules.
A submission captures an immutable and identifiable revision.
Later draft edits never silently alter content already under review.

milestones.experiment: Open a review screen, edit the requester's draft elsewhere, then compare both records. Verify the reviewer still sees the submitted snapshot.
milestones.review: Avoid using one generic update endpoint for every lifecycle transition. Explicit commands make permissions and side effects easier to inspect.
milestones.stretch: Add a diff between the latest draft and the last submitted revision.

milestones.title: Express reviewer eligibility as rules
milestones.brief: Assign reviewers using an explicit policy that prevents disallowed self-approval and explains why an action is unavailable.
milestones.explanation: Eligibility can depend on requester, role, team, request type, and current assignment. Put the policy in a testable service rather than duplicating conditions across buttons and routes. A UI explanation may be friendly, but the command must evaluate current policy again using verified identity.
steps: Write a decision table for requester, assigned reviewer, unassigned staff, delegate, and administrator. Include self-approval and missing assignments.
Implement eligibility checks with explicit denial reasons and use the same policy at assignment and decision boundaries.
Test every table row through direct service calls, then verify the UI displays only appropriate actions without treating visibility as enforcement.

checks.label: Eligibility matches the decision table for all representative actors.
Disallowed self-approval is rejected at the command boundary.
Role or assignment changes take effect on the next command.

milestones.experiment: Load a review page, revoke its assignment, then submit a decision from that stale page. Verify current policy rejects it.
milestones.review: Ask the agent to identify the source of every policy input. Request body fields must not manufacture an actor's role or assignment.
milestones.stretch: Version the policy used for a submission so a later rule change remains explainable.

milestones.title: Commit one decision per review revision
milestones.brief: Accept an authorized decision for the displayed submission revision and reject conflicting or repeated commands predictably.
milestones.explanation: A decision targets a specific review state. Two browser tabs can submit contradictory results, and a lost response can cause a retry. Combine revision/state comparison with a unique operation identity and store the decision and state transition transactionally. A retry with different decision content must not reuse the old operation ID silently.
steps: Define accepted, already-decided, stale-revision, and denied outcomes. Specify whether one or several approvals are required.
Implement the conditional decision transaction with audit data and a stable operation receipt. Preserve the reviewer's reason if the request fails.
Race approve and reject commands, retry after a lost response, and attempt to approve a superseded submission.

checks.label: Conflicting decisions cannot both silently finalize one review state.
Retrying the same operation does not duplicate the decision.
A stale submission is identified without discarding the reviewer's draft reason.

milestones.experiment: Pause approve and reject after authorization, then release both. Inspect the final submission state and every decision row.
milestones.review: Point to the database condition that protects finalization. A service-level read followed by an unconditional update leaves the race unresolved.
milestones.stretch: Extend to two required reviewers and prove that final approval occurs only after the required distinct decisions commit.

milestones.title: Support bounded delegation
milestones.brief: Allow a reviewer to delegate eligible work for a limited interval without granting unrelated authority or losing the original assignment history.
milestones.explanation: Delegation changes who may act, not necessarily who originally owned the obligation. Define its scope, start/end boundaries, revocation behavior, and whether re-delegation is permitted. Evaluate current delegation at command time, and retain both acting identity and delegation provenance in the decision record.
steps: Model a delegation window and permitted request scope. Write cases for future, active, expired, revoked, and out-of-scope delegation.
Implement create/revoke delegation with authorization and a controllable clock. Display why the delegate has access without impersonating the original reviewer.
Test decision submission at both time boundaries and after revocation while a review screen remains open.

checks.label: Delegates can act only inside the declared scope and interval.
Revocation prevents future decisions from stale screens.
Stored decisions identify the real actor and delegation source.

milestones.experiment: Have a delegate begin a decision before expiry and finish afterward. Verify the documented commit-time policy determines the outcome.
milestones.review: Explain why copying the delegator's user ID into the command would destroy accountability. Keep identity and authorization provenance separate.
milestones.stretch: Prevent delegation cycles if the product permits chains, and show the effective authorization path.

milestones.title: Explain a request's complete history
milestones.brief: Build a timeline connecting draft submissions, assignment changes, withdrawal, delegation, and decisions to their exact revisions.
milestones.explanation: Current status answers what is true now; history explains how it became true. Record the revision and actor for each accepted transition so reviewers can reconstruct the path. A timeline projection should tolerate removed display names and remain protected by the request's access policy.
steps: Define structured events and the minimum fields needed to reconstruct each lifecycle transition. Avoid storing credentials or unnecessary draft content.
Commit events with state changes, expose a stable paginated read, and render links to the relevant submission snapshots.
Withdraw and resubmit a request, change its reviewer, then decide. Verify the timeline tells that sequence accurately after reload and export.

checks.label: Every accepted lifecycle transition points to the correct revision.
Unauthorized actors cannot read request history through timeline endpoints.
Missing profile details do not break historical attribution.

milestones.experiment: Give several events the same timestamp. Verify the timeline uses a stable tie-breaker and does not reshuffle after pagination.
milestones.review: Distinguish an activity projection from the authoritative decision records. If a projection is rebuilt, the underlying history should still support the same explanation.
milestones.stretch: Add a reconciliation check that detects finalized requests whose required decision evidence is missing.

milestones.title: Verify notifications and release recovery
milestones.brief: Ship the approval workflow with duplicate-safe notifications and a migration rehearsal that preserves in-flight reviews.
milestones.explanation: A workflow deployment must consider records halfway through the process. Changes to status names, required reviewers, or snapshot formats can strand active requests. Test old in-flight fixtures against the new build, keep notification intent separate from provider delivery, and define rollback in terms of readable data as well as code versions.
steps: Create fixtures for a draft, submitted request, delegated review, partially approved request, and finalized request. Declare the supported upgrade behavior.
Add notification outbox entries to accepted transitions and test delivery retries against a fake provider. Recheck current relevance before sending stale jobs.
Migrate a database copy, run each workflow forward, then rehearse rollback. Restore a backup into an isolated environment and verify its history.

checks.label: In-flight fixtures remain actionable after migration.
Provider failure does not erase a committed decision.
Rollback and restore preserve readable snapshots and decision provenance.
